printed_headline_estimate: Municipality-level Robust Paired Samples T-Tests (5-year pre vs. 5-year post cadastral update; N = 33 municipalities with complete utility data out of 53 studied): (1) Water coverage (Cobertura acueducto, Table 5, PDF p. 13 & text p. 16): statistically significant increase (p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.82) in 5/33 municipalities (15.15%; e.g., Palestina t = -8.572, df = 2.00, p = 0.013, d = 0.9777; Montenegro t = -11.867, df = 2.00, p = 0.007, d = 0.8856; Quimbaya t = -11.926, df = 2.00, p = 0.007, d = 0.8879; Manizales t = -7.004, df = 2.00, p = 0.020, d = 0.9629; Armenia t = -5.678, df = 2.00, p = 0.030, d = 0.8244) and null in 28/33 (84.85%); water subscribers increased significantly in 8/33 (24.24%, p < 0.05, d > 0.77). (2) Sewerage coverage (Cobertura alcantarillado, Table 6, PDF p. 14 & text p. 16): statistically significant increase (p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56) in 22/33 municipalities (66.67%; e.g., Pereira t = -29.212, df = 2.00, p = 0.001, d = 0.906; Manizales t = -19.379, df = 2.00, p = 0.003, d = 0.892; Armenia t = -8.345, df = 2.00, p = 0.014, d = 0.918) and null in 11/33 (33.33%); sewerage subscribers also increased significantly in 22/33 (66.67%). (3) Drinking-water quality risk index (IRCA, Table 7, PDF p. 15 & text p. 16, N = 42 municipalities): significant increase in risk in 12/42 (28.57%, p < 0.05, d > 0.87) and null in 30/42 (71.43%).
publication_year_note: Published in Bitácora Urbano Territorial, Vol. 34, No. 1 (Marzo - Junio 2024), pp. 97-114; Received 21/10/2023, Accepted 26/12/2023. No separate online-first publication year appears on the PDF.
rationale: The full text (in Spanish, with English/Portuguese/French abstracts) empirically evaluates municipal cadastral updating (actualización catastral, mandated every 5 years under Colombia's Ley 1450 de 2011 Art. 24 and tied to property tax valuation and SSPD/SGP utility coverage certification under Ley 1176 de 2007 and Decreto 416 de 2007) across municipalities in Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda. Using JAMOVI's Walrus Robust Paired Samples T-Test comparing 5-year pre-update vs. 5-year post-update periods, the author reports inferential t-statistics, degrees of freedom, p-values, and Cohen's d effect sizes for water (acueducto) subscribers and coverage (Table 5, N = 33 municipalities) and sewerage (alcantarillado) subscribers and coverage (Table 6, N = 33 municipalities), alongside municipal property tax revenue (Tables 2-3), SGP water/sanitation intergovernmental transfers (Table 4), and IRCA drinking-water quality risk (Table 7). Although no pooled panel regression is estimated across municipalities, the municipality-specific pre-post inferential t-tests and vote-count synthesis proportions (15.15% positive significant for water coverage; 66.67% positive significant for sewerage coverage) directly test an administrative/fiscal/institutional-capacity rule mechanism (Family C, adjacent to land-cadastre administration in Family A) on household/property water and sanitation coverage outcomes (Criterion 4), making it SWiM-eligible.
